title: Review: Centripetal force; Electric field strength and field lines; Coulomb's law; Electric potential and potential energy
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C02-1#N.15, F02-1#N.8a, F03-1#N.11, F04-1#N.10a, C02-1#N.4a, F02-1#N.12b, F03-1#N.2, F04-1#N.5a, C02-1#N.3a, F02-1#N.4. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Coulomb's law
items.clue: Rule that two point charges interact in proportion to their product and to 1/r².

items.label: Electric potential
items.clue: Quantity V, zero at infinity by definition, that falls as 1/r around a single charge.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Kind of quantity with a sign but no direction, so several values add as plain numbers.

items.label: Centripetal force
items.clue: Inward mv²/r needed for circular motion, supplied by a real pull such as that of a string.

questions.stem: A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.

questions.stem: Three point charges are fixed on the x-axis: P (+4.0 nC) at x = 0, Q (+1.0 nC) at x = 0.10 m and R (+2.0 nC) at x = 0.30 m. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the magnitude of the resultant electric force on Q?

The field lines of a long, straight charged wire spread out radially, in planes at right angles to the wire: they spread in two dimensions, not three. Point P is 2.0 cm from the wire and point Q is 6.0 cm from it, both far from the wire's ends. How does the electric field strength at P compare with that at Q?

options.text: E at P is 9 times E at Q, as the field strength falls with the square of the distance.
E at P is 3 times E at Q, as the same lines spread over 3 times the area at Q.
E is the same at P and Q, as every line that passes P also passes Q.
E at Q is 3 times E at P, as the larger cylinder at Q holds more lines.

questions.stem: In a region of uniform electric field of strength 4.0 × 10³ V m⁻¹ directed in the +x direction, point A at x = 0 has an electric potential of +500 V. What is the electric potential at point B, at x = 0.050 m?

A car travels at constant speed around a bend on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts towards the centre and is the resultant force.
Friction acts towards the centre and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act towards the centre.
A forward driving force along the bend is the resultant force on the car.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres exert electric forces of magnitude F on each other. The charge on each sphere is halved, and the distance between them is reduced to one third of its value. What is the magnitude of the force now?
questions.explanation: Force ∝ (product of the charges)/r². Charges: ½ × ½ = ¼. Distance: 1/(⅓)² = 9. New force = 9F/4 ≈ 2.3F.

questions.stem: At point P, a charge of +2.0 µC experiences an electric force of 5.0 × 10⁻³ N directed east. This charge is removed and a charge of −6.0 µC is placed at P; the charges that produce the field do not move. Taking east as positive, what is the electric force on the −6.0 µC charge?

A point charge of +5.0 nC is fixed in place. A second charge of +2.0 nC is moved slowly from a point 0.30 m from the fixed charge to a point 0.10 m from it. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the work done on the +2.0 nC charge by the external force?
A cyclist rides around a flat circular track at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about her motion is correct?

options.text: Her velocity is constant, so the resultant force acting on her is zero.
Her velocity changes, so a resultant force acts towards the centre.
A resultant force acts on her outwards, away from the centre of the track.
A resultant force acts on her forwards, along her direction of motion.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres whose centres are 0.60 m apart exert electric forces of magnitude 1.0 N on each other. Their charges do not change. At what centre-to-centre separation would the forces have a magnitude of 9.0 N?
